Solution 3 (Manual Ordered Pairing [MOP])[edit]

A sum of consecutive odd positive integers can also be represented as an arithmetic sequence, in this case, with common difference 2 and the first term being odd. The sum of an arithmetic sequence can also be represented as the product of the average term in the sequence and the number of terms. Therefore, we have . We know that the number of terms must be even, since if it was odd, then the sum of the sequence would be an odd number. We also know that the average term of the sequence must be even, because since there are an even number of terms, then the average term is the median of the two "middle" terms, which must be even. Therefore, we must have it such that and multiply to 60, while both factors have to be even. This gives ordered pairs with being the average term of the sequence and being the number of terms: . However, gives an arithmetic sequence with some numbers in the sequence being negative, and since the problem specifies we need positive integers, we discard this case. Similarly, doesn't work either. The other cases work though, so we have a total of cases. ~Baihly2024
